The conclusion is false, so no argument could establish it; but the specific unjustified inference is s9, which observes that the sweep covers [1, 3881] and then asserts the statement for every n in [1, 37570]. Nothing in s1-s8 bridges (3881, 37570]. Steps s3-s8 are true but inert filler (n^3-n=120 at n=5; n^2>=2n on [2,2000]; (n-3)n^2=(n-3)H(n); n^3 = n mod 6; 4|n implies n(n+1)/2 even; existence of n<=2000 with n^2>2000) -- none of them mentions the Collatz map or bounds any stopping time. The verifier confirms the argument's own swept range is clean (max stopping time on [1,3881] is 237, at n=3711), so the defect is precisely the unbridged extrapolation, and the first failure past the sweep is n=17647.
